text: Sreeja is a Graduate Research Assistant at DePaul University (Sep 2025 to present), working on harmonic persistence barcodes for machine learning. Her research sits at the intersection of topology and machine learning. Topological data analysis studies the shape of data: loops, voids, and connected components that survive across scales. She works on harmonic persistence barcodes, a way of enriching these topological signatures with geometric information carried by harmonic chains. Concretely, she implements matrix-based algorithms in Python that turn mathematical specifications into clean, tested code, and runs experiments comparing these enriched barcodes against traditional persistence features on shape classification tasks. Early results are promising, and a publication is in preparation. The code is private while the work is under way, but she's happy to talk about it in detail. Related tools/topics: Topological Data Analysis, Persistent Homology, GUDHI, Linear Algebra, Python.
short: Her research is on harmonic persistence barcodes — basically finding ways to make topological data analysis capture more geometric detail than it normally would. She writes the algorithms herself in Python, and she's working on turning it into a publication.

topic: AI Policy RAG

topic: Malicious Prompt Detector
text: The Malicious Prompt Detector classifies LLM prompts as benign or malicious using a stacked ensemble model trained on 39,000 labeled prompts. Built with NLP techniques, scikit-learn, focused on AI safety. Live demo: https://huggingface.co/spaces/Sreeja-reddy/malicious-prompt-detector
